title: Operational feedback lab journal — compiled asks and quick patches (Dec 2027)
body:
Purpose: quick synthesis of recurring operational asks from enterprise customers (Dedicated + Private) collected during Dec 2027 field calls and support threads. This is intentionally pragmatic — raw quotes, small patches we can ship fast, and higher-risk asks for product/engineering prioritization.

Context: multiple customers running mixed workloads (batch embedding, low-latency chat, scheduled bulk reranking) reported pain across four surface areas: unpredictable tail latency, surprise billing from cache misses, lack of deployment-level rollout observability, and debugging friction for request-level routing/fallbacks. Notes below mix verbatim snippets, short triage, and proposed next actions with rough effort estimates.

Raw customer snippets (anonymized):
- "One minute spike on 99.9th percentile when we hit larger context windows — our users see timeouts." — fintech-cust-A
- "Billing shows X of cache-miss tokens but we have no visibility into why cache dropped. We suspect model swaps during canaries." — enterprise-cust-B
- "Our compliance team needs an audit trail showing which model variant served each request and when the route fell back to a cheaper variant." — healthcare-cust-C
- "We tried the Dedicated burst option and still saw requests routed to hosted pool — that's unacceptable for our SLA." — platform-cust-D

Observed patterns and short analysis: 
1) Tail latency correlates with mixed sequence length workloads and occasional KV cache invalidations (likely due to model reloads or shard rebalancing). Customers with a heavy prefix reuse pattern suffer most.
2) Billing confusion stems from token accounting across cache hits/misses and transparent quantization variants — customers see attractive unit cost on quote but higher monthly bill when cache usage dips.
3) Rollouts: canary traffic shifts sometimes trigger model variant mismatches across regions; the control plane UI lacks a clear per-route timeline + model-variant breadcrumb for audits.
4) Debugging pain: SRE and customer support cannot reconstruct request-level route decisions (why a request went to fallback model/region) because traces are not tied to model-variant metadata in logs available to customers.

Actionable quick patches (low effort, high impact) — aim to ship within 2–4 sprints:
- Patch A: Add a per-request model_variant header in responses (both hosted and Dedicated) with a compact code (e.g., mv=redwood-13b-q4) and surface in logs available to customer tenants. Owner: eng-support. Effort: 1 sprint.
- Patch B: Expose simple cache-hit rate metric at token granularity and surface rolling-7d in Console per-route. Owner: observability. Effort: 2 sprints.
- Patch C: Billing note: attach cache-hit-adjusted cost estimator in invoices (show tokens billed vs tokens saved). Quick UI/CSV add-on for finance teams. Owner: finance+console. Effort: 1 sprint.
- Patch D: Fail-open policy doc fragment for Dedicated: small doc + default enforcement to avoid routing to hosted when a tenant has explicit 'dedicated-only' flag. Owner: product-dedicated. Effort: 1 sprint + small infra guardrail.

Medium-risk proposals (needs product/eng reprioritization):
- Proposal 1: "Route replay" tool in Console — ability for tenant admins to replay a sample of recent requests to see exact model variant decisions and token accounting. Ties into request-level logs and stored KV snapshot. Benefits: audits, root-cause of cache misses. Rough effort: 6–8 weeks.
- Proposal 2: Per-route rollback timeline + model-variant mapping — a time-series UI showing rollouts, canary percent, region routing, and which model build was active. Also expose an API for programmatic audits. Rough effort: 8–12 weeks.
- Proposal 3: Heuristic KV-stability mode for long-prefix workloads — the runtime can prioritize keeping cache pinned to shards during canaries/rollouts for tenants that opt in (tradeoff: memory overhead). Need research + perf testing. Rough effort: exploratory spike (3 wks) + implementation (8–12 wks).

Priority matrix (quick view):
- P0 (ship this month): Patch A (model_variant header), Patch B (cache metrics), Patch C (billing transparency)
- P1 (next quarter): Patch D (dedicated-only guardrail), Proposal 1 (route replay)
- P2 (longer term): Proposal 2 (rollback timeline + API), Proposal 3 (KV-stability mode)

Open questions to resolve (notes to self):
- Which teams own the customer-facing log retention increase if we surface per-request headers? Cost implications? (ask infra + finance)
- Secure surface: do we show model_variant in clear or hashed form for regulated tenants? (ask security/compliance)
- Are there existing audit hooks in Private deployments we can reuse for per-request routing metadata? (infra-private)

Suggested next steps / runbook for CS reps:
1) For each large account hitting tail latency, enable detailed request-logging toggle (manual) and capture a 24h trace window. Tag traces with reason codes (cache-miss, model-swap, rebalancing).
2) Offer the billing transparency CSV to finance contacts and walk through the cost delta explanation; push Patch C as a confidence-building measure.
3) For Dedicated customers complaining of misrouting, confirm their 'dedicated-only' setting and escalate to platform-engineering if requests were served by hosted pool. Log incidents and attach sample request ids.

Stakeholder notes / owners:
- eng-support: Patch A (lead: Evan Brooks)
- observability: Patch B (lead: Priya Kapoor)
- finance + console: Patch C (lead: Luis Martinez)
- product-dedicated: Patch D (lead: Sanjay Rao)
- infra-private: consult for Proposal 3 (lead: Anika Desai)

Appendix — snippets from support threads (verbatim, redacted):
- "We had a spike during a bulk rerank job. Console shows 95th p 120ms but 99.9th at 1.8s; end users hit front-end timeouts — guessed it was cache churn when we scaled. Any way to lock cache?" (ticket CS-5923)
- "Invoice line items are hard to reconcile. Show us tokens billed vs tokens sent — our legal team needs a deterministic mapping." (email thread subject: invoice-dispute-enterprise-B)

Notes to self: keep this doc alive and mark 'snapshot' dates when we push patches. Once Patch A lands, circle back and collect impact metrics (expected reduction in time-to-resolution for incidents by ~30%).

Links for reference: CONFLUENCE:ops-feedback-lab-2027 (full field notes), JIRA:CS-5923 (tail-latency-case), GITHUB:pull/2287 (early proto for model_variant header).
